subject: MPO cross-account commit and approval gates
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Priya Suresh <priya.s@nimbus.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@nimbus.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MPO cross-account commit and approval gates

Hi Priya / Tom —

Thanks for walking us through Nimbus' buyer topology yesterday. A couple of proposals to keep the MPO moving without adding extra procurement cycles: 

1) Term options: offer a 6-month pilot (cross-account, limited seats) that can auto-convert to a 12-month commitment if usage > 75% of forecast over the pilot window, or become a standard 36-month discounted MPO with a separate exec signoff. This gives the buyer a low-friction pilot path while preserving the option for a longer term if they want price predictability.

2) Buyer approval gates: recommend a two-step internal approval at Nimbus — procurement + BU finance for pilots under $50k, procurement + centralized procurement committee for anything > $50k or multi-AZ entitlements. Can you confirm who signs for multi-account acceptance?

3) Marketplace mechanics: we'll need the AWS seller rep to confirm whether the pilot can be scoped as a private offer across 2 linked accounts under the same organization ID, and whether auto-conversion to a longer MPO is supported on the listing (we've seen variations across accounts).

Attached: Redwood_MPO_Term_Options_v1.pdf — very lightweight, shows pricing bands and conversion mechanics.

Next steps: if this looks reasonable, can you share the internal contact who will approve pilots? If you want, we can draft the DocuSign MPO with a pilot appendix.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0119
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Suresh <priya.s@nimbus.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@nimbus.com>
Date: 2027-09-13T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MPO cross-account commit and approval gates

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear options. A few notes from procurement:

- Nimbus prefers a short pilot (6 months) for platform-level purchases; that aligns with our risk committee.
- Approval matrix: for pilots up to $40k, BU head + procurement is sufficient. Anything above that routes to our vendor committee (monthly meeting).
- For cross-account setups: legal will want the MPO to explicitly list the linked accounts by account ID and include a rollover clause rather than an "automatic" conversion without signoff.

Can you send a draft MPO that includes the linked-account appendix and a rollover clause (30-day notice for conversion)? Also loop in your AWS seller contact so we can confirm listing constraints.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Suresh
Senior Procurement Manager, Nimbus Systems
priya.s@nimbus.com | +1 212-555-2250

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-09-14T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MPO cross-account commit and approval gates

Priya — thanks, clear. Attached is a short MPO draft that implements your asks:

- Pilot appendix: lists two linked account IDs (redacted in this draft) and scope of entitlements.
- Rollover clause: pilot converts to a 12-month commitment if usage threshold (>=75% of forecast) is reached and signed within 30 days; otherwise the pilot can either renew as another 6-month pilot or lapse.
- Approval language: we added a signatory block for the BU head + procurement for pilots <= $40k and vendor committee for > $40k.

Two logistics asks for Nimbus: please provide the exact AWS account IDs to add to the appendix, and confirm the BU head name for the signature block.

I've also opened a HubSpot deal record (see link) and can push a DocuSign powerform once we confirm account IDs: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/98765

Attachment: Redwood_MPO_DRAFT_72m.pdf (pilot appendix & rollover clause included).

If that works, I'll loop in AWS seller to confirm the listing behavior and timing — Vivek, Ben, can you help confirm marketplace timeline with AWS and any seller-side listing constraints?

Best,
Jordan
